what_it_does: Cloud servers run many tenants' workloads, but some of the server's processor cores are consumed by the cloud provider's own housekeeping software — things like scheduling which task runs next, managing memory, and handling network requests. Those stolen cores reduce the revenue-generating compute available to paying customers. SmartNICs (network interface cards with their own ARM processor cores built in) sit inside the server and could do this housekeeping instead. Wave is a software framework that moves existing Linux userspace system programs — with little or no code change — onto those SmartNIC ARM cores, freeing the main server cores for tenant work. It adds a fast communication channel between the SmartNIC and the host so decisions that must happen in microseconds (like which thread runs next) still happen quickly enough.
